source: Every philosopher examined a position. Therefore there is one position that every philosopher examined.

claims.interpretation_note: The author assumes this universal statement implies a single shared position, though the premise could also be interpreted as each philosopher examining a distinct position.

claims.text: There is one position that every philosopher examined.

evidence.quote: Therefore there is one position that every philosopher examined.

ambiguities.issue: Ambiguity in the scope of 'a position' in the premise
alternatives: Each philosopher examined a unique position (distinct from others)
All philosophers examined the same single position

translations.formula: (forall x (implies (Philosopher x) (exists y (and (Position y) (Examined x y)))))
translations.reason: Translates 'Every philosopher examined a position' as universal quantification over philosophers, each with an existential quantifier for their position

translations.formula: (exists y (and (Position y) (forall x (implies (Philosopher x) (Examined x y)))))
translations.reason: Translates 'There is one position that every philosopher examined' as existential quantification for the shared position, with universal quantification over philosophers

interpretation_notes: The premise C1 allows for multiple distinct positions (one per philosopher) while the conclusion C2 requires a single shared position. The formalization preserves this ambiguity in the premise's scope without resolving it.
The translation uses first-order logic with explicit quantifier scope to represent the two possible interpretations of C1 mentioned in the reconstruction's ambiguities section.
